questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: What is the HCF of 26 and 91?
questions.solution: 26 = 2 × 13 and 91 = 7 × 13. The only common prime factor is 13, so HCF = 13.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: What is the LCM of 12 and 18?
questions.solution: 12 = 2² × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3². LCM takes the highest powers: 2² × 3² = 36.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If HCF(a, b) = 4 and a × b = 96, then LCM(a, b) is:
questions.solution: HCF × LCM = a × b, so LCM = 96 ÷ 4 = 24.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Which of these numbers is irrational?
questions.solution: √4 = 2, 0.25 = 1/4 and 3/7 are all rational. √2 cannot be written as p/q, so it is irrational.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: What is the HCF of 2³ × 3² and 2² × 3³?
questions.solution: HCF takes the lowest power of each common prime: 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: n² − 1 is always divisible by 8 when n is:
questions.solution: If n is odd, n − 1 and n + 1 are consecutive even numbers, so one of them is a multiple of 4. Their product (n − 1)(n + 1) = n² − 1 is then a multiple of 2 × 4 = 8. For even n, n² − 1 is odd.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Check whether 6ⁿ can end with the digit 0 for any natural number n.
questions.solution: A number ends in 0 only if it is divisible by 10 = 2 × 5. 6ⁿ = 2ⁿ × 3ⁿ has no factor 5, and by the uniqueness of prime factorisation it never will. So 6ⁿ can never end with 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the HCF and LCM of 6, 72 and 120 using prime factorisation.
questions.solution: 6 = 2 × 3, 72 = 2³ × 3², 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5. HCF = lowest common powers = 2 × 3 = 6. LCM = highest powers of all primes = 2³ × 3² × 5 = 360.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that √5 is irrational.
questions.solution: Assume √5 = a/b with a, b coprime integers, b ≠ 0. Then a² = 5b², so 5 divides a², hence 5 divides a. Write a = 5c: 25c² = 5b², so b² = 5c² and 5 divides b. Then 5 divides both a and b, contradicting that they are coprime. So √5 is irrational.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Given that √3 is irrational, show that 5 − √3 is irrational.
questions.solution: Assume 5 − √3 = r is rational. Then √3 = 5 − r. Since 5 and r are rational, 5 − r is rational, so √3 would be rational. This contradicts the given fact, so 5 − √3 is irrational.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: What is the degree of the polynomial 5x³ − 2x + 7?
questions.solution: The highest power of x is 3, so the degree is 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The zeroes of x² − 9 are:
questions.solution: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3), which is 0 when x = 3 or x = −3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The sum of the zeroes of x² − 5x + 6 is:
questions.solution: Sum of zeroes = −b/a = −(−5)/1 = 5.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The product of the zeroes of 2x² − 8x + 6 is:
questions.solution: Product of zeroes = c/a = 6/2 = 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A polynomial of degree 2 is called a:
questions.solution: Degree 1 is linear, degree 2 is quadratic and degree 3 is cubic.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If 2 is a zero of x² + kx − 6, what is k?
questions.solution: Put x = 2: 4 + 2k − 6 = 0, so 2k = 2 and k = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Which quadratic polynomial has zeroes −2 and 5?
questions.solution: Sum = −2 + 5 = 3 and product = −10, so the polynomial is x² − (sum)x + product = x² − 3x − 10.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If α and β are the zeroes of x² − 4x + 3, then α² + β² is:
questions.solution: α + β = 4 and αβ = 3. α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 16 − 6 = 10.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the zeroes of x² − 2x − 8 and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
questions.solution: x² − 2x − 8 = (x − 4)(x + 2), so the zeroes are 4 and −2. Sum = 2 = −(−2)/1 = −b/a. Product = −8 = −8/1 = c/a. Verified.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find a quadratic polynomial whose sum of zeroes is −3 and product of zeroes is 2.
questions.solution: A quadratic is x² − (sum)x + (product) = x² − (−3)x + 2 = x² + 3x + 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If α and β are the zeroes of x² − 6x + 8, find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are 2α and 2β.
questions.solution: α + β = 6 and αβ = 8. New sum = 2α + 2β = 12. New product = 4αβ = 32. The polynomial is x² − 12x + 32.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Which of these is a quadratic equation?
questions.solution: x³ − 4x = 0 has degree 3, 2x + 5 = 0 has degree 1, and (x + 1)² = x² + 2 simplifies to 2x − 1 = 0. Only x² + 3x − 4 = 0 has degree 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the discriminant of 3x² − 2x + 1/3 = 0 and state the nature of its roots. Find the roots if they are real.
questions.solution: D = (−2)² − 4 × 3 × (1/3) = 4 − 4 = 0, so the roots are real and equal. x = −b/2a = 2/6 = 1/3 (both roots).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A train travels 360 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 5 km/h more, it would have taken 1 hour less for the same journey. Find the speed of the train.
questions.solution: Let the speed be x km/h. 360/x − 360/(x + 5) = 1, so 360 × 5 = x(x + 5), i.e. x² + 5x − 1800 = 0. This factorises as (x + 45)(x − 40) = 0. Speed cannot be negative, so the speed is 40 km/h.
